text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key idea is to use clear naming conventions. Choose names that explain what a variable or function does, such as "totalPrice" instead of "x". Another important point is to keep functions small and focused on one task. This makes them easier to test and reuse. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain. When you or your team need to fix a bug or add a feature later, readable code saves time and reduces mistakes. In short, writing clean code helps everyone.
